extraction.name: CoNLL-2003 Named Entity Recognition Dataset
extraction.description: Language-independent named entity recognition data for English and German, concentrating on four types of named entities: persons, locations, organizations, and names of miscellaneous entities that do not belong to the previous three groups.
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang, Fien De Meulder
extraction.citeAs: Tjong Kim Sang, E. F., & De Meulder, F. (2003). Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was taken from existing corpora: the Reuters Corpus for English and the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus for German.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English data from the Reuters Corpus; German data from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus (Frankfurter Rundshau).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: English: August 1996 to August 1997; German: August 1992 to December 1992.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Linguistic preprocessing was applied: tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, and chunking. English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger. German data was lemmatized, tagged, and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp. Mostly MUC conventions were followed. An extra named entity category called MISC was added. Named entities are assumed to be non-recursive and non-overlapping; when a named entity is embedded in another, usually only the top level entity has been annotated.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Named entities are assumed to be non-recursive and non-overlapping. When a named entity is embedded in another named entity, usually only the top level entity has been annotated.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development (tuning), and testing of named-entity recognition systems.
